items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: I was playing with Mulligan... Nick Travis was calling the guys... Nick was first trumpet player with the band.

ctx.x: What kind of money were you making with that group?

I asked for a little more money and he paid it, and then he resented it. So we had a little tete-a-tete. At one point I was playing with Mulligan for I guess a year and he was going to go to Europe. So Nick Travis was calling the guys. He was acting as personnel manager. Nick was first trumpet player with the band. And I was offered a Broadway show, I was offered “Music Man.” It was running already but the first trombone player was leaving and the conductor wanted me to come in and play. So I had that as a…
Yeah. Did you have to pay your own way, I mean like your own meals and all that kind of stuff?
